assets.name: lecture_04_figure_01.png
assets.rationale: The completed radial equation is visible with both the angular kinetic contribution and the potential derivative.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: This extra term is what is usually called the centrifugal force.

assets.name: lecture_04_figure_02.png
assets.rationale: The polar equations and angular conservation law are assembled in a stable board state.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: The momentum conjugate to theta is constant.

assets.name: lecture_04_figure_03.png
assets.rationale: The substituted radial equation displays the inverse-cube centrifugal barrier clearly.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: This term gets very big when r gets small.
assets.caption_hint: effective radial equation at fixed angular momentum

assets.name: lecture_04_figure_04.png
assets.rationale: The completed endpoint form of the Noether variation is legible and minimally occluded.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: The equations of motion make the integral term vanish.
assets.caption_hint: Noether variation reduced to its endpoint term

assets.name: lecture_04_figure_05.png
assets.rationale: The common x translation and the resulting sum of particle momenta are both visible.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: The conserved quantity is the total momentum in the x direction.

assets.name: lecture_04_figure_06.png
assets.rationale: The rotational generator and angular-momentum combination are complete on the board.

assets.name: lecture_04_figure_07.png
assets.rationale: The shifted trajectory, sign of the induced displacement, and endpoint geometry appear together.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: At fixed time the new trajectory samples the old one at an earlier time.

assets.name: lecture_04_figure_08.png
assets.rationale: The Hamiltonian definition and its one-dimensional energy check are simultaneously visible.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: For the familiar Lagrangian the Hamiltonian is kinetic plus potential energy.
